The .SRCINFO file presents a conventional AUR package definition for nautilus-typeahead. It pulls the upstream Nautilus source from the official GNOME GitLab via git+https, references a pinned commit in libgxdp, and includes two small patches that restore typeahead functionality. Dependencies, package relations, and checksums (b2sums) are listed normally. No obfuscated code, dangerous commands (eval, curl|bash, etc.), or unexpected network destinations are present. The sole referenced install script (post.install) is not included in the provided excerpt, so its content cannot be evaluated; however, the visible metadata shows no red flags. Overall, the file follows standard AUR packaging practices and contains no evidence of injected malicious code.

The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices. It retrieves Nautilus and libgxdp from GNOME infrastructure, applies local patches, modifies a schema setting to enable typeahead behavior, builds with Meson, and installs files into the package directory. The libgxdp source is pinned to a specific commit, while the Nautilus source uses a version tag. Checksum entries, local patch application, the install hook, and the file-splitting helper present no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscated commands, unexpected remote execution, or malicious system modification.
